claim: The recovered 1584 byte frag1.dat has the right length, so the recovery is complete.
observation: E03 export _rag1.dat is 1584 bytes but MD5 c4f3b9a0f17d464f4fc61b94ecf6cc21 does not match the reference 7a3bc5b763bef201202108f4ba128149. E04 frag1.dat is 1584 bytes with MD5 7a3bc5b763bef201202108f4ba128149 (match).
image_and_location: E03: deleted entry start cluster 2 (sector 88), size 1584, FAT[2]=0, FAT[2..12] all 0; E04: MFT 29, $DATA 128-3, runs 4073(1)+4075(1).
reasoning: Length and name only show a same-sized output. In FAT the chain is cleared on deletion, so a tool can only assume consecutive clusters (2,3); cluster 3 is the start of deleted _rag2.dat. Publisher map sectors 88-89 then 92-93 means 1584-1024 = 560 bytes from the second extent. NTFS keeps the run list, so E04 needs no assumption.
limitation: Autopsy version and reconstruction method are not documented; the published sector map is test ground truth, not something the FAT metadata preserves. Single tool, single image pair.
next_check: Record the Autopsy version; compare with a second tool; check whether the recovered bytes of E03 differ from the reference in the second extent only.
